John: Hi Tim! Congrats on your success! Keep it up, you're doing great! I'm also trying out yoga to get a little extra strength and flexibility. It's challenging but worth it.
Tim: Thanks! I appreciate your encouragement. How's it going with yoga? Have you noticed any improvements?
John: Yoga's been really awesome for me. It's helped me improve in terms of strength and flexibility, as well as focus and balance during my workouts. It's been great!
Tim: Great news! Yoga is indeed amazing for your body and mind. Are there any specific poses that you enjoy practicing?
John: Yeah, there are a couple of poses I really enjoy. Warrior II makes me feel strong and there's one that helps with balance and stability. I love how these poses challenge my body and mind!
Tim: Woohoo! Congrats on finding poses that suit you. Yoga is so cool for showing us what we can really do. Maybe you could share a pic so I can try it too?
John: Here's a photo of me in this pose. It's a good way to work out your legs and core. Give it a shot!
Tim: That's a tough one! How long do you usually hold that pose?
John: I typically hold it for 30-60 seconds. It really helps with building strength and stability!
Tim: That's cool, I'm gonna give it a shot and see how it goes. Thanks for the tip!
John: No worries! Let me know how it goes. Happy to help whenever you need it!
Tim: Thanks! Your support and encouragement have truly made this journey better. I really appreciate it.
John: I'm here for you. You've got this!
Tim: Thanks! Your support means a lot to me. Your friendship means a lot too.
John: Thanks, I really appreciate it. Your friendship means a lot to me too.
Tim: Glad we're friends! Plus, bonus points for both being into fantasy books and movies. I just reorganized my book shelf, speaking of.
John: Cool! Can I take a closer peek at it? What are some of your favorites?
Tim: Yeah, check it out - here's my bookshelf! I have some of my favorites on there, like these ones. It's an amazing journey!
John: That bookshelf is awesome! The Hobbit is one of my favorites too. What an amazing journey!
Tim: Glad you like it! The Hobbit is great, but have you read that other popular fantasy series? It's also awesome!
John: Yeah, I've read that other popular fantasy series too! It's one of my favorites. It has such a cool story!
Tim: It's awesome how these books take us to different worlds!
John: It's like escaping to these incredible new worlds and having a break from reality for a fun adventure.
Tim: Yeah, that's why I love them. They let us take a break from reality and have an awesome adventure. So magical!
John: Yeah, it's awesome! Like being transported to a different world with all those amazing moments - so fun!
Tim: Wow, what an awesome shot! Feels like a magical forest - where was that?
John: The photo is from a forest near my hometown. It's so tranquil.
Tim: Wow, nature's amazing! We're lucky to have places like that near our homes.
John: It's incredible how we have these beautiful places near our homes. We should definitely appreciate them.
Tim: It really does have a way of calming us and reminding us of the beauty around.
John: Definitely! It grounds us and makes us appreciate the simple beauty around us. We should take time to enjoy it.
Tim: That picture looks super peaceful! It reminds me of a trip I took last summer.
John: We had a blast camping and disconnecting from the everyday.
Tim: Looks great! Where did you go camping?
John: We went camping in the mountains and it was stunning! The air was so refreshing.
Tim: Sounds great! Being in the mountains is the best. What was your favorite part of it?
John: I loved just chilling and taking in the beauty of nature. It was super peaceful and refreshing.
Tim: Yeah, nature has that effect on me too. It's like a reset for the soul.
John: Yeah, nature's great for clearing the mind and calming the soul. This was my Rocky Mountains trip last year and it was stunning. Seeing those mountains, fresh air - it makes you realize how incredible the world is.
Tim: Wow, this is amazing! Nature is really awesome - it makes us feel tiny but connected.
John: Nature does have a way of humbling us and showing us our place in the world. It's truly amazing and comforting.
Tim: Yeah. It reminds us that we're not alone - we're part of something bigger. Bye!

selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains multiple instances of encouragement and support between Tim and John, such as Tim congratulating John on his yoga progress and John offering support to Tim during his yoga journey. This directly aligns with the skill's purpose of extracting offers, encouragement, and advice.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.
